author: Al Jazeera English
description:
US-Israeli Strikes on Iranian infrastructure have intensified fears of wider political and environmental consequences as the conflict escalates. Oil facilities, refineries and water infrastructure have reportedly been targeted across the country.
Foad Izadi, a professor at the University of Tehran’s Faculty of World Studies, told Al Jazeera that the United States and Israel are attempting to destabilise Iran and potentially divide the country.
He pointed to comments by Donald Trump suggesting Iran’s map may change, arguing this indicates plans to “Balkanise” the country and separate oil-rich regions along the Persian Gulf.
Izadi said such a strategy would require weakening Iran’s leadership and political system to create internal collapse.
He added that many Iranians blame the United States and Israel for the attacks rather than their own government.
Izadi also said more than 1,400 civilians have reportedly been killed since the strikes began.
He warned attacks on oil facilities ahead
title: Iranian academic warns US and Israel aim to ‘Balkanise’ Iran

description:
A limited number of flights are resuming to Doha as airlines try to move stranded passengers between the Gulf and Europe.
Only a few dozen passengers were on board one of five Qatar Airways flights returning to the Qatari capital.
The disruption follows widespread airspace closures across the Middle East.
More than 23,000 flights have been cancelled, with losses estimated in the hundreds of millions of dollars.
The crisis is also disrupting air freight and global logistics, with Qatar Airways among the world’s largest cargo carriers.
Aviation experts warn the disruption could have lasting effects just as the industry was recovering from the COVID-19 pandemic.
The crew says fighter jets may accompany aircraft approaching Doha to ensure safety.
